evidence.observation: The lifecycle orchestrator. If options.resolveProjectTrust is supplied it runs the pre-trust pass first (line 451-455): loadProjectTrustExtensions() produces preTrustExtensions, the callback decides trust, and setProjectTrusted(projectTrusted) stores it. It then calls settingsManager.reload() (line 458) to re-read settings for that trust state, resolves package/CLI paths, and calls loadFinalExtensionSet(extensionPaths, preTrustExtensions) (line 512) for the post-trust pass. After extensions it loads skills, prompts, themes, context files, and system prompt, ending with this.loaded = true (line 603). Without a resolveProjectTrust callback there is no pre-trust pass and no trust flip.

The pre-trust bootstrap pass. It deliberately forces settingsManager.setProjectTrusted(false) and reloads so that project-scoped settings/packages/extensions stay excluded, then returns loadCurrentExtensionSet({ includeInlineFactories: true }). This yields a trust-minimal extension set: user/global extensions plus temporary CLI extensions and inline factories only, which is what the resolveProjectTrust callback receives.

The post-trust pass. With no preTrustExtensions it just cold-loads extensionPaths plus factories and diagnostics. With a preTrustExtensions result it indexes those extensions by resolvedPath and skips any path already preloaded or already failed (lines 652-663), loading only the remaining (newly trusted project) paths while reusing preTrustExtensions.runtime (line 668). It reorders extensions to the final extensionPaths order, re-appends inline (<inline:...>) extensions, and merges errors/warnings, so a user extension executes exactly once across both passes.

Backs the pre-trust pass. It resolves package paths and CLI extension sources in temporary scope, merges them (honoring noExtensions), builds a metadata map, collects host-package warnings, loads via loadExtensionsCached, and conditionally appends inline extension factories when includeInlineFactories is true. It is trust-independent of project extension overrides, which is why it is safe to run before a trust decision.

Shows a post-trust trust gate. The project SYSTEM.md path (cwd/.pi/SYSTEM.md) is only returned when settingsManager.isProjectTrusted() is true and the file exists; otherwise discovery falls back to the global agentDir/SYSTEM.md. discoverAppendSystemPromptFile (lines 1107-1119) applies the same isProjectTrusted() gate to APPEND_SYSTEM.md. reload() calls these at lines 583-592, i.e. after the trust state has been set.

The trust decision function passed as reload's resolveProjectTrust. Precedence: an explicit trustOverride wins (line 47-49); if hasTrustRequiringProjectResources(cwd) is false it returns true without prompting (line 50-52); otherwise it emits the extension project_trust event via emitProjectTrustEvent and honors a returned result, persisting it when result.remember is true (lines 54-70); then a stored trustStore decision is used (lines 72-75); then defaultProjectTrust 'always'/'never' resolves (lines 77-84); finally, with no UI it returns false (lines 86-88) or prompts via selectProjectTrustOption and saves the selection (lines 90-95).

The interactive branch of the trust decision. It enumerates getProjectTrustOptions(cwd, { includeSessionOnly: true }) and asks ctx.ui.select with formatProjectTrustPrompt(cwd) (lines 24-26), matching the chosen label back to a ProjectTrustOption. This is the only path that requires hasUI; resolveProjectTrusted returns false without UI, so headless runs default to untrusted.

Supporting evidence for what the trust flip does. Setting projectTrusted=false clears projectSettings to {} and recomputes settings from global only, while setting it true (re)loads project settings from storage. This is the mechanism by which the pre-trust pass excludes project resources and the post-trust pass admits them; reload() (lines 539-565) re-reads settings using the current this.projectTrusted.

Supporting evidence for the trust short-circuit. It returns true only when trust-requiring project config resources exist under cwd/.pi or a .agents/skills directory in cwd or an ancestor (excluding the user-global ~/.agents/skills). resolveProjectTrusted calls it at project-trust.ts:50 to skip the whole trust decision when no project resources need trust.

claims.claim: DefaultResourceLoader.reload runs a two-pass extension lifecycle gated on a resolveProjectTrust callback: a pre-trust bootstrap pass (loadProjectTrustExtensions, which forces setProjectTrusted(false) and loads only user/global, temporary CLI, and inline extensions) followed by the trust decision, then a post-trust pass (loadFinalExtensionSet) that reuses the pre-trust extensions and loads only the remaining, newly trusted project paths.

The pre-trust pass excludes project-scoped extensions so project code cannot run before the user consents: loadProjectTrustExtensions calls settingsManager.setProjectTrusted(false) and reload(), and settingsManager.setProjectTrusted clears projectSettings so only global settings apply at that point.

Pre-trust-loaded extensions are not re-executed after trust is granted: loadFinalExtensionSet indexes preTrustExtensions by resolvedPath, filters those and previously failed paths out of the remaining set, loads the remainder into the same runtime, and restores final ordering, so a user extension's side effects run exactly once.

resolveProjectTrusted resolves trust in a fixed precedence order: explicit trustOverride, then true when no trust-requiring project resources exist, then an extension-provided project_trust event result, then a persisted trustStore decision, then the defaultProjectTrust policy, and finally an interactive prompt that yields false when no UI is available.

Trust gates project-scoped content beyond extensions: after trust is applied, discoverSystemPromptFile only selects project cwd/.pi/SYSTEM.md and discoverAppendSystemPromptFile only selects cwd/.pi/APPEND_SYSTEM.md when settingsManager.isProjectTrusted() is true, otherwise they fall back to the global agentDir copies.

conclusion: The resource-loading lifecycle in packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts is a trust-gated, two-phase process. When reload() receives a resolveProjectTrust callback it performs a pre-trust pass: loadProjectTrustExtensions() calls settingsManager.setProjectTrusted(false) + reload() so that only user/global settings, temporary CLI extension sources, and inline factories are visible, then loadCurrentExtensionSet({ includeInlineFactories: true }) loads that trust-minimal extension set. The callback (resolveProjectTrusted in project-trust.ts) then decides trust with the precedence trustOverride > no trust-requiring project resources (hasTrustRequiringProjectResources) > extension project_trust event > stored trust.json decision > defaultProjectTrust policy > UI prompt (false when headless); the result is stored with setProjectTrusted and settings are reloaded. The post-trust pass re-enters loadFinalExtensionSet(extensionPaths, preTrustExtensions): it reuses the already-loaded extensions and runtime by resolvedPath, loads only the newly admitted project paths, restores ordering, and re-adds inline extensions, guaranteeing each extension executes once. After that, skills, prompts, themes, context files, and system/append-system prompts are resolved, with project-scoped system prompts (cwd/.pi/SYSTEM.md, APPEND_SYSTEM.md) admitted only when isProjectTrusted() is true. Without a resolveProjectTrust callback there is no trust flip and the loader follows the single cold-load path.
